subject.title: Workboard dispatch hardcodes execution.engine to "codex" (mismatch with actual worker routing)

question: Should `execution.engine` represent the resolved provider/harness that executed the run, while the card keeps its separate OpenClaw `agentId`, or should the existing two-value execution-engine contract remain a display abstraction?
rationale: `agentId` is an arbitrary OpenClaw agent identity, whereas the execution field is persisted and currently restricted to `codex | claude`; choosing its durable meaning determines the safe repair and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Record resolved runtime identity
options.body: Pass the runtime/provider identity resolved for the started subagent run into Workboard metadata and preserve agent targeting separately.

options.title: Retain a constrained display enum
options.body: Keep `execution.engine` as a limited display category and add explicit metadata for the routed agent/runtime instead of overloading the field.

recommendation.title: Record resolved runtime identity
recommendation.body: Pass the runtime/provider identity resolved for the started subagent run into Workboard metadata and preserve agent targeting separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The only concrete ownership signal available is the adjacent report that already documented the same cross-runtime contract gap.
